briefs.title: Exact maximum product for uniformly cross-intersecting families: prove P_3(n) = 20 * 2^(n-6) for all n >= 6 (and, if the mechanism extends, P_4(n) = 70 * 2^(n-8))
briefs.statement_and_quantifiers: For integers l >= 0 and n >= 2l, let P_l(n) be the maximum of |A||B| over all pairs (A, B) of families of subsets of [n] with |A \cap B| = l for EVERY A in A and B in B (exact intersection, not >=). Conjecture (Ahlswede-Cai-Zhang, restated in OWR 2006/48 p.45): P_l(n) = binom(2l, l) * 2^(n-2l). BRIEF TARGET: the exact statement for l = 3, all n >= 6: P_3(n) = 20 * 2^(n-6); optionally l = 4: P_4(n) = 70 * 2^(n-8). Lower bound is witnessed by: fix B0 = [2l], A = {S : |S \cap B0| = l} (|A| = binom(2l,l) 2^{n-2l}), B = {B0}; symmetric variants.

briefs.title: Every simultaneous (p,q)-core partition is contained in the maximal (p,q)-core kappa_pq
briefs.statement_and_quantifiers: Let p, q be coprime positive integers. Let kappa_pq denote the unique partition of maximal size (p^2-1)(q^2-1)/24 that is both a p-core and a q-core (existence and uniqueness: Olsson-Stanton). CLAIM TO PROVE: the Young diagram of EVERY partition lambda that is simultaneously a p-core and a q-core is contained in the Young diagram of kappa_pq (i.e. lambda_i <= (kappa_pq)_i for all i).

source.primary_literature: Anderson's bijection between (p,q)-cores and (p,q)-Dyck paths (Anderson, 'Partitions which are simultaneously t- and (t+1)-cores', 2002, and the rational (m,n) version, e.g. arXiv:1504.02075 retained extract-level at sources/393907/); Olsson-Stanton max-size theorem as cited in arXiv:2610.35322 ('Olsson and Stanton [10, Theorem 4.1] found the unique core of largest size') and arXiv:1502.07934.
source.status: The OWR record poses containment as open (2006). This session's public searches (2026-10-30 UTC) found the uniqueness/max-size theorem but no public proof or disproof of universal containment; this is record-level evidence, not an exhaustive clearance. briefs.full_scope_mechanism: Beta-set characterization: lambda is an s-core iff its beta-set beta(lambda) = {lambda_i + len(lambda) - i} is downward s-closed (a in beta, a >= s implies a-s in beta) — this is the criterion validated by the in-lane computation against Anderson's counts. Route: (1) for coprime p,q, the (p,q)-cores are exactly the partitions whose beta-sets arise from (p,q)-Dyck paths via Anderson's bijection; (2) the maximal core kappa_pq corresponds to the greedy (topmost) Dyck path (all north steps first); (3) prove the monotonicity lemma: if Dyck path P_2 lies pointwise weakly below P_1, then the core of P_2 is contained in the core of P_1 (via the beta-set/abacus description, the beta multiset of the greedier path dominates elementwise, which is equivalent to Young-diagram containment); (4) every (p,q)-Dyck path lies pointwise weakly below the greedy path; (5) conclude, using Olsson-Stanton only to identify the greedy core's size with (p^2-1)(q^2-1)/24. Alternative self-contained route avoiding the path bijection: prove directly that if lambda is a (p,q)-core then lambda_i <= (kappa_pq)_i by induction on abacus runners (each runner of a p-abacus of a (p,q)-core is forced below the maximal configuration).
briefs.decisive_small_calculation: Already run and retained: work/verify_core_containment.py enumerates all partitions of size <= 45 (540,634 + empty), tests s-coreness via the beta-set criterion, and checks, for all 15 coprime pairs (p,q), p<q<=13 with (p^2-1)(q^2-1)/24 <= 45: (a) core counts match 1/(p+q) binom(p+q,p) EXACTLY (validates the s-core criterion and enumeration against Anderson's theorem); (b) the largest core has size exactly (p^2-1)(q^2-1)/24 (validates against Olsson-Stanton); (c) every core is contained in the max core. All 15 pairs pass; no counterexample. This makes a false conjecture unlikely at small scale and pins the mechanism.
briefs.expected_certificate_size: Small: a 3-6 page proof (beta-set downward-closure lemma + one monotonicity lemma + greedy-path identification); machine-checkable control = the retained enumeration JSON (a few hundred KB); Lean endpoint needs only finite combinatorics and integer arithmetic; only propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound anticipated.
briefs.formal_dependencies: Definitions of partitions, hook lengths/beta-sets, Anderson's bijection (or the direct abacus route), Olsson-Stanton max-size theorem (citable; or reproved directly for the greedy path). No analysis.
briefs.strongest_classical_adaptation_objection: The containment may be folklore-known or follow immediately from a published characterization of (p,q)-cores as exactly the partitions contained in kappa_pq in some reference the searches missed — if such a characterization exists, the result is a known theorem and earns no credit.
